name: git stash
shortDescription: Temporarily shelf (stash) changes to your working directory so you can switch branches without committing incomplete work.
detailedDescription:
The `git stash` command takes your uncommitted changes (both staged and unstaged), saves them away for later use, and reverts your working directory to match the HEAD commit. 

This is invaluable when you're in the middle of a feature and an urgent bug report comes in. You can't switch branches with a dirty working directory, but your work isn't ready for a commit. `git stash` gives you a clean slate.

Stashes are stored in a stack (LIFO - Last In, First Out). You can have multiple stashes saved, and you can apply them to any branch, not just the one where you created them.
syntax: git stash [push | pop | apply | list | drop | clear]

parameters.description: Save current changes to the stash. The default action if no subcommand is given. Using `-m` adds a description to help identify it later.
Remove the most recent stash from the stack and apply it to the current working directory.
Apply a stash to the working directory, but KEEP it in the stash list. Useful if you want to apply the same changes to multiple branches.
Remove a specific stash from the list.
When stashing, also include untracked files (new files you haven't run `git add` on yet).

examples.title: Basic stash workflow
examples.description: Save work, fix a bug on another branch, then restore the work.
examples.code:
git stash push -m "WIP: new login form"
git checkout main
# ... fix bug, commit ...
git checkout feature-branch
git stash pop

examples.title: List and apply specific stashes
examples.description: If you have multiple stashes, you can pick which one to apply.
examples.code:
git stash list
# stash@{0}: WIP: new header
# stash@{1}: WIP: footer changes

git stash apply stash@{1}

examples.title: Stash everything, including new files
examples.description: By default, stash ignores untracked files. Use -u to grab everything.

commonMistakes.text: If `git stash pop` results in merge conflicts, it will NOT remove the stash from the list. You must resolve the conflicts, commit, and then run `git stash drop` manually.
Stashes are local to your repository. They are not pushed to the remote server.
